summary: Describes a URN namespace for the Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG), used to give persistent names to things produced as part of the MPEG standards. Examples include technical documents, XML schemas, classification schemes, namespaces, style sheets and media assets. It registers the naming scheme rather than defining a protocol.

eli5.summary: Movie folks have lots of files, forms and rule books. This document gives them a special way to write permanent names for each one, like a label that never changes, so anyone can find the right item.

questions: what is the mpeg urn namespace
how does mpeg assign persistent names
subtitle: A permanent naming system for standards and resources produced by MPEG.

tldr.problem: The Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG) produces many standards and related resources like XML schemas, classification schemes, and specifications. These resources need persistent, globally unique names that do not change when servers or formats change.
tldr.mechanism: A URN namespace named urn:mpeg is registered with a two-level hierarchical structure: urn:mpeg:{standard name}:{assigned string}. MPEG controls all assignments and maintains catalogs mapping URNs to resources.
tldr.outcome: MPEG can assign and resolve persistent names to its standards and resources, supporting discovery, resolution, and identification services.

facts.label: Standard names covered
facts.value: mpeg1, mpeg2, mpeg4, mpeg7, mpeg21, and future standards

today: RFC 3614 is Informational and remains the formal URN namespace registration for MPEG. The namespace is maintained by the Motion Picture Experts Group for naming resources, schemas, and specifications produced as part of MPEG standards development.

sections.title: MPEG and Its Resource Naming Needs
sections.content:
The Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG) is a working group of ISO and IEC that develops international standards for coded representation of digital audio and video. MPEG has produced MPEG-1 (foundation for Video CD and MP3), MPEG-2 (foundation for DVD and digital television), MPEG-4 (multimedia for the web), MPEG-7 (multimedia content description), and is developing MPEG-21 (multimedia framework).

MPEG produces many resources beyond protocol specifications: XML schemas, classification schemes, identification systems, technical documents, and other standards-related materials. To make these resources discoverable and persistent, MPEG requested a formal URN namespace. A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a persistent, location-independent identifier that can be resolved to find the actual resource, no matter where it is stored.
sections.eli5: MPEG makes video standards and tools. They need permanent names for each schema, document, and definition so people can find them anywhere.

sections.title: URN Structure and Naming Hierarchy
sections.content:
MPEG URNs follow the form urn:mpeg:{standard name}:{assigned US-ASCII string}. The standard name corresponds to an MPEG standard like mpeg1, mpeg2, mpeg4, mpeg7, or mpeg21. The assigned string is any US-ASCII string that conforms to URN syntax.

For example, valid MPEG URNs include urn:mpeg:mpeg7:schema:2001 and urn:mpeg:mpeg7:cs:GenreCS:2001. The standard name is case-insensitive for matching purposes, meaning MPEG7 and mpeg7 refer to the same standard. Everything after the standard name is case-sensitive.

Uniqueness is guaranteed as long as the assigned string is never reused for a given standard and the standard name itself is never reassigned. Each URN is assigned through the development process of the MPEG standards.
sections.eli5: Names look like urn:mpeg:mpeg7:myresource. The first part says what MPEG standard, the second part says what specific thing. MPEG decides what gets a name.

sections.title: Assignment, Resolution, and Persistence
sections.content:
MPEG controls all URN assignments, though it may designate portions of its namespace for assignment by other parties (such as registration authorities for MPEG-7 classification schemes). Individual URNs are assigned through the normal MPEG standards development process.

MPEG develops and maintains URN catalogs that map all assigned URNs to Uniform Resource Locators (URLs), enabling Web-based resolution of named resources. In the future, MPEG may develop an interactive online resolution system to automate the process. The presence of a URN in a catalog indicates that it is valid.

MPEG is committed to maintaining the accessibility and persistence of all resources officially assigned URNs. This commitment depends on proper delegation at the standard-name level and persistence of standard-name assignments. MPEG may authorize additional resolution services as needed.
sections.eli5: MPEG keeps a directory mapping each permanent name to where the file actually is. Anyone can ask MPEG 'where is this name?' and get pointed to the resource.

sections.title: Types of Resources and Services
sections.content:
Resources that can be named include XML Schema Definition files, classification schemes, identification systems, and other materials produced as part of MPEG standards. The namespace is broad enough to cover the full range of MPEG's output.

Services that can be supported include controlled term lookup in classification schemes and resolution of identifiers in identification systems. As MPEG standards evolve and new resource types are produced, the namespace can accommodate them without modification, since MPEG controls the structure and can add new standard names as needed.
sections.eli5: MPEG can name schemas, lists of categories, identification codes, and anything else it produces. People can use the names to look things up.

sections.title: Community and Future Development
sections.content:
With ongoing development of MPEG standards, MPEG establishes requirements for assignment and use of identifiers within the namespace. For example, registration authorities have responsibility for processing third-party requests to register MPEG-7 classification schemes. MPEG continues to develop reference software implementations to help clients resolve and use URNs in MPEG standards.

This URN namespace allows MPEG to maintain persistence and discoverability of its resources over time, supporting the international multimedia standards community in adopting and implementing MPEG specifications.
sections.eli5: MPEG keeps adding new standards, and the naming system grows with them. The permanent names ensure that old and new resources can always be found.
